extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, advocacy groups, industry, and organizations preparing comments for DOT/NHTSA rulemakings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments to DOT/NHTSA notice-and-comment rulemakings, including where to submit, timing, and what content is most influential. Useful for individuals and organizations who want their comments to be considered in the agency's final rulemaking decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments can be submitted through https://www.regulations.gov, or at the Docket Management Facility located at the U.S. Department of Transportation. Use the docket identified in the NPRM to ensure your comment is associated with the correct rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment period timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical and variable lengths of the public comment period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, agencies allow 60 days for public comment. Sometimes they provide much longer periods, and they may use shorter periods where they can provide justification for them. The public may request more time; providing justification helps the agency decide whether to extend or reopen the comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments provide empirical evidence supporting the commenter's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments that provide empirical evidence get the most attention. Comments that merely state an opinion without supporting evidence are reviewed but generally have little impact on the agency's final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive issues that can change agency decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of comment content likely to prompt agency reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA (and agencies generally) may reconsider a rule if a comment addresses material errors of fact or law, raises new evidence, or cites practical difficulties in complying with the proposed rule. Focus comments on concrete errors, new data, and implementation/practicability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the NPRM for specific procedures and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking for case-specific instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific procedures and comment deadlines for each proposed rule are typically included in the NPRM published in the Federal Register. Check the NPRM for docket numbers, submission instructions, and any rule-specific requirements.
